title: ADHD, Autism & Neurodivergent Experience
description: Explore neurodiversity as population variation through dialogue, evidence and psychological reasoning.

lessons.title: Different minds, same task
lessons.teach: Follow the conversation one message at a time. Notice what the behaviour might be achieving before you decide why it happened. About five minutes.
lessons.objective: Distinguish observable evidence from a tentative explanation of neurodiversity as population variation.

nodes.title: What might be happening?
nodes.body:
Neurodiversity describes variation within human populations rather than one person's fixed profile. A person's contribution depends partly on the fit between their needs and the environment. A structured speaking order can improve access without lowering the intellectual demands of the meeting.

An accommodation preference does not establish a diagnosis. Different people with the same diagnosis can need different arrangements.

nodes.title: Try a different response
nodes.prompt: The goal is to improve the situation without pretending that you can read the person's mind.
nodes.explanation: A proportionate response deals with the actual situation: Trial an agenda and structured turn-taking, then review whether participation improves. Its value does not depend on the other person accepting an interpretation of their motives.
nodes.counterexample: Some situations require independent support or safer channels rather than another direct conversation. An accommodation preference does not establish a diagnosis. Different people with the same diagnosis can need different arrangements.

lessons.title: What would change your mind?
lessons.teach: An initial explanation is useful only if it can be challenged. Revisit the characters, test a rival account and apply the idea in another setting. About five minutes.
lessons.objective: Test an account of neurodiversity as population variation with new evidence and transfer it to a new case.
